question.problem:
The curvature of the plane curve $r(t)={e}^{t}\,i+2t\,j$ is given by 

$$
κ(t)=\frac{2{e}^{t}}{\bbox[2pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAA}}}.
$$

 
What is the missing part of the expression?
question.worked_solution:
The curvature $κ(t)$ of a plane curve $r(t)=x(t)\,i+y(t)\,j$ is given by

$$
κ(t)=\frac{|{x}^{′}(t){y}^{″}(t)-{y}^{′}(t){x}^{″}(t)|}{([{x}^{′}(t)]^{2}+[{y}^{′}(t)]^{2})^{3/2}}.
$$

Along our curve, we have

$$
x(t)={e}^{t},\,y(t)=2t.
$$

First, we calculate the derivatives of the components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & ={e}^{t},\, & {y}^{′}(t) & =2 \\ {x}^{″}(t) & ={e}^{t},\, & {y}^{″}(t) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting these into the formula for the curvature, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{|{e}^{t}\cdot 0-2\cdot {e}^{t}|}{{(({e}^{t})^{2}+{2}^{2})}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{|-2{e}^{t}|}{{({e}^{2t}+4)}^{3/2}} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{({e}^{2t}+4)^{3}}}\end{aligned}
$$
